correctness.rationale: Renewal at the first reset gives the immortal transform 1/(1+qA(q+ρ)); independent exponential mortality tilts this transform to φρ(m+u)/φρ(m), normalized by the probability of success. Logarithmic differentiation gives V−M²=−(2A′+mA″)/(1+mA). Since A″=H/(4z⁶)>0 for z>0 by H′=e^z(z²−3z+3)>0 and H(0)=0, the sign of CV−1 is that of B(z)−m, with z=√(m+ρ). Expanding the numerator of B′ gives G/z²=−6 plus positive powers with positive coefficients: g₄,…,g₁₀ are positive directly, and for n≥11 P(n)≥30 and a doubling induction shows 30·2ⁿ>16n³+320n. Thus G/z² has one positive simple zero, and B has a strict nondegenerate maximum; B″(zc)=−4zcG′(zc)/H(zc)²<0. At the boundary z=√m the sign follows from B(z)−z²=z³e^z(1−z)/H(z). Together with B(1)=1, zc>1, mc<zc², and the subsequent zero of B, this proves the counts and signs, including the excluded zero-rate equality at m=1 and the admissible double root at mc. The high-precision independent check recovered mc≈1.10642822093643738483 and ρc≈0.28424024613180761599 and both rates at m=1.05; it compared moments at 12 parameter pairs.
